title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
authors: Shunta Takahashi, Zhi Li, Beni Yoshida
abstract: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers. Geometrically, the proof locally emulates the unavoidable crossing between electric and magnetic strings, similar to a cross-cap in a non-orientable manifold. Extending the problem to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code, we find that an order-two Clifford realization exists for odd $N$, whereas it is impossible for even $N$. Our results show that the group law of an emergent electromagnetic duality need not lift faithfully to its microscopic Clifford realization.
summary: This paper proves that the natural order-two electric-magnetic duality symmetry in the toric code cannot be realized by a simple, local Clifford unitary operation for the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case. It generalizes this to $\mathbb{Z}_N$ codes, finding that the order-two realization fails for even $N$, demonstrating a deep link between the symmetry's algebraic structure and the underlying lattice topology.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the electric-magnetic (e-m) exchange duality, which has order two in the anyon types of the toric code, can be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford unitary operation.
main_result: For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, no locality-preserving Clifford realization of the e-m exchange can have order two. Furthermore, for the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ code, an order-two realization is only possible for odd $N$.
method: The proof uses geometric arguments involving string crossings, relating the unitary operator's action on stabilizers to topological features analogous to a cross-cap.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code on a lattice, characterized by vertex and plaquette stabilizers ($A_v$ and $B_p$). The core object of study is the unitary operator $U_{em}$ implementing the e-m exchange.
key_observables: The order of the unitary operator $U_{em}$ (or its dressed version $W$) acting on the physical Hilbert space, and the commutation relations between local Pauli operators under this transformation.
important_parameters: The integer $N$ defining the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ code, and the lattice structure (e.g., $L_x \times L_y$ periodic boundary conditions).
main_assumptions: The primary theorem assumes locality-preserving realizations of the e-m exchange. The general proof avoids assumptions about translation symmetry or fixed stabilizer pairings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the anyon excitations, the conjugation rules for Pauli operators under $U_{em}$, and the string geometries used in the proof, relating the obstruction to topological crossings.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case, proving the order-two impossibility. It then generalizes to $\mathbb{Z}_N$, establishing the odd/even dependence. The methodology involves analyzing the action of the symmetry on stabilizers using Pauli symplectic formalism and geometric string arguments.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental relationship between abstract topological symmetries (like e-m duality) and their physical realization within quantum error-correcting codes, which is central to quantum computation theory.
